packages.evidence: Provider capability matrix, documented test/sandbox path, cost/onboarding record and treasurer selection decision.
packages.external_inputs: Committee-authorized processor account/KYC, treasurer identity, current service terms and approved costs are external inputs. Start this package early in parallel after its dependencies.

packages.title: Implement approved donation policy and election configuration
packages.scope: Create versioned treasurer-approved configurations for committee identity, election designations/dates, effective limits, campaign-specific exclusions, donor attestations, record fields, recurring caps and remedy workflows. Define authoritative aggregation across processor and offline records with concurrency handling and conservative reconciliation of uncertain identities.
packages.acceptance: No 2025-2026 number is hard-coded as a 2028 rule. Campaign choices such as age 18 and no PAC money are preserved without being mislabeled universal law. Stale/missing approval disables fundraising. Frontend checks are not the enforcement boundary; provider-direct and recurring paths are covered or explicitly blocked.
packages.evidence: Configuration approval tests, concurrency/cycle boundary fixtures, donor-identity ambiguity tests and treasurer-reviewed policy matrix.
packages.external_inputs: Treasurer/election-counsel approval of applicable rules is required before live fundraising.

packages.title: Integrate hosted checkout with the approved donation design
packages.scope: Wire homepage amount/frequency selection and the dedicated donation page to processor-hosted fields or a reviewed embedded checkout. Keep the campaign-owned shell visually faithful; use supported theming for the secure form. Preserve amount, frequency, election designation and consent when entering checkout without leaking donor PII in URLs. Provide a trusted hosted fallback when embedding is blocked.
packages.acceptance: Card numbers/CVV never reach campaign servers, logs or analytics. Unchecked eligibility, invalid amounts or unapproved election configuration stop the flow. Closing/retrying/back navigation cannot silently duplicate a gift or switch its frequency. External handoff is clear and does not introduce a second unapproved recipient.
packages.evidence: Sandbox checkout journeys, iframe/hosted fallback accessibility, network inspection and amount/designation tampering tests.

packages.title: Implement authenticated, idempotent payment webhooks
packages.scope: Validate the provider signature over exact raw request bytes before JSON processing; enforce account/page allowlists, size bounds and supported event types. Durably accept events, deduplicate, redact/drop unnecessary donor fields and route financial changes into the outbox/ledger. Apply replay/state-order protections without assuming the provider supplies a signed timestamp.
packages.acceptance: Invalid signatures and wrong-account events never alter records. Duplicate, delayed, reordered and replayed valid events cannot double count or roll state backward. Server crash after receipt causes safe replay; success is never inferred from a browser return URL.
packages.evidence: Provider signature vectors, raw-body corruption tests, event-order/replay suite and webhook crash/retry evidence.

packages.title: Implement the contribution ledger and reconciliation
packages.scope: Add append-only financial events and audited projections for gifts, fees, payouts, election allocations, refunds, disputes and recurring installments. Use integer minor units, unique provider identifiers and explicit made/received/settled dates. Reconcile with provider reports and the treasurer-authorized accounting source, including other contribution channels.
packages.acceptance: Ledger totals reconcile to source reports; missing/disputed events are flagged rather than concealed. Gross/net/fee totals are distinct. Name/email alone never establishes that two donors are the same. Correcting a record adds an audit event instead of overwriting financial history.
packages.evidence: Reconciliation fixtures, duplicate/partial refund cases, currency precision tests and treasurer comparison report.

packages.title: Implement receipts and recurring donor self-service
packages.scope: Connect the processor donor portal or supported API for receipts, recurring schedule visibility, cancellation and supported payment-method updates. Keep donor and volunteer accounts independent; an optional explicit link must be verified. Disclose frequency, next charge and cancellation effect and respect provider authority for final state.
packages.acceptance: A donor can cancel through the documented working path without joining the volunteer system. Replayed clicks do not create new commitments. Recurring limits/expiry rules apply before future charges through a proven provider mechanism; unavailable enforcement is a launch gap, not hidden behavior.
packages.evidence: Create/renew/cancel/retry sandbox scenarios, receipt accuracy and unauthorized donor-portal access tests.

packages.title: Implement finance exception and remedy workflows
packages.scope: Provide treasurer-only review of suspect/prohibited/excessive gifts, missing contributor information, refunds, disputes, chargebacks, cancellations and authorized redesignation/reattribution records. Model deadlines from the approved ruleset and store documentary evidence. Use generic donor notifications and approved provider actions, not direct card handling.
packages.acceptance: An ordinary admin cannot refund, reallocate or access donor identity. Partial refunds and disputes reconcile correctly. Best-efforts follow-up is bounded and recorded; the software does not falsely certify legal sufficiency. Donor intent/election records are preserved.
packages.evidence: Exception lifecycle tests, deadline fixtures, role enforcement and treasurer-reviewed remedy scenarios.

packages.title: Implement controlled treasury reporting and exports
packages.scope: Generate treasurer-approved exports for the chosen accounting/FEC filing workflow, with review, reconciliation totals, schema validation and evidence references. Limit PII to authorized recipients, log exports and apply approved retention. Keep public campaign analytics aggregate only; do not create a public donor directory.
packages.acceptance: Exports reconcile to ledger/source reports and preserve required designation/receipt information. CSV formula injection and unauthorized/bulk extraction are blocked. No filing is submitted automatically and no export is labeled an accepted FEC filing.
packages.evidence: Export golden files, schema/total validation, injection tests and a treasurer import dry run.
packages.external_inputs: The treasurer must identify the actual accounting/filing system and approve its mapping.

packages.title: Harden and test the full donation system
packages.scope: Exercise card-testing/abuse controls using provider-supported protections, rate limits and no sensitive fingerprinting. Test unavailable provider, stale rules, parallel donations, excessive recurring schedules, conflicting identities, cancellations, refunds, chargebacks, webhook exhaustion, reconciliation outage and accessible fallback.
packages.acceptance: The site never shows payment success before authenticated confirmation. Failure states preserve clear donor choices and never silently retry a charge. Direct hosted links obey campaign restrictions. All requested exclusions are accounted for through configuration, attestation and treasurer review without claiming perfect automatic detection.
packages.evidence: Donation threat-model review, adversarial/sandbox suite, error-state screenshots and data-leak inspection.

packages.title: Complete treasury and fundraising release acceptance
packages.scope: Have the authorized treasurer verify committee identity, processor onboarding, bank/payout setup, disclosures, effective election configuration, donor-field collection, receipts, cancellation, remedies, exports, retention and reconciliation ownership. Record approval against the exact build/configuration and expiry/review triggers.
packages.acceptance: Fundraising cannot enable unless evidence and responsible contacts exist. A code/config change affecting compliance invalidates the relevant approval. Sandbox tests are distinct from any later expressly authorized small live transaction; developers do not charge a card merely to claim completion.
packages.evidence: Signed/attributed treasury checklist, configuration digest, processor acceptance evidence and documented live-test authorization process.
packages.external_inputs: Actual committee/treasurer decisions and credentials are required; developers cannot manufacture this approval.

packages.title: Implement retention, privacy requests and secure lifecycle cleanup
packages.scope: Implement per-class retention, account closure, consent withdrawal, authorized data access/export, deletion jobs and legal holds. Delete expired temporary files, token records and cache entries safely. Treat required financial retention separately from ordinary profile deletion. Backups have documented expiry and key custody.
packages.acceptance: Account deletion never promises to erase legally retained finance records or downloaded copies. No one can request another persons data by changing an ID. Cleanup is restart-safe, logged minimally and tested against protected-object/key references and active legal holds.
packages.evidence: Retention/deletion fixtures, legal-hold tests, privacy-request identity checks and backup-expiry runbook.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Implement privacy-preserving campaign measurement
packages.scope: Add aggregate public page/action counts and operational conversion measurements with documented definitions. Exclude session replay, ad pixels, cross-site tracking, hidden fingerprints and political profiling. Do not instrument protected form fields, reports, donor identity or individualized issue histories. Separate security logs from campaign measurement.
packages.acceptance: Staff can see that signup/checkout delivery is functioning without inspecting peoples private interests or messages. Opt-out/consent settings are respected. Dashboards display real data with sampling/latency caveats, not mock numbers.
packages.evidence: Event allowlist tests, network/PII canaries, log-retention checks and dashboard metric definitions.

packages.title: Complete accessibility across public and authenticated journeys
packages.scope: Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA with automated and manual testing: keyboard, screen readers, headings, focus, errors/status announcements, accessible authentication, targets, contrast, reflow/zoom and reduced motion. Review media captions and audio description where relevant; transcripts alone do not satisfy every video criterion. Include third-party checkout and video failures.
packages.acceptance: No unresolved blocker prevents a user from reading issues, joining, using materials, completing forms or donating. Accessibility fixes preserve the design. Any third-party limitation has a genuinely accessible working alternative and an owner, not only a disclaimer.
packages.evidence: Manual audit report, automated results, assistive-technology journey recordings and issue closure evidence.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Complete visual fidelity and cross-browser regression testing
packages.scope: Compare the eight approved views and newly required operational screens at mobile/tablet/desktop widths, including 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 pixels. Test Chromium, Firefox and WebKit/Safari with stable fonts and motion frozen for screenshots. Review the explicit video amendment separately from unchanged baseline sections.
packages.acceptance: No accidental redesign, cropped portrait/hand, overflow, broken navigation, unreadable disclosures or dashboard-like public homepage remains. Snapshot updates require an explanation; a failing comparison cannot be fixed solely by approving the new image.
packages.evidence: Before/after visual report, cross-browser runs, approved amendment baseline and documented design exceptions.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Meet performance, resilience and load budgets
packages.scope: Optimize responsive images, selective hydration, deferred third-party content, caching, bundle splitting and API/database queries. Load-test authentication, library, task claims, document delivery and donation-event ingestion. Test slow networks, disabled JavaScript on public content, provider delays and database connection pressure.
packages.acceptance: Target public-page p75 LCP <=2.5s, INP <=200ms and CLS <=0.1 when sufficient field samples exist; use documented lab conditions before launch. Keep public initial compressed JS approximately <=100KB, excluding user-activated providers, unless a reviewed budget exception is justified. Slow services fail visibly without corrupting data.
packages.evidence: Lab measurements, load/recovery tests, bundle budget report and later field-measurement plan; targets are not preclaimed results.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Complete application security review and remediation
packages.scope: Run dependency/secret scans, authorization/CSRF/XSS/SSRF/upload tests, browser egress and supply-chain review, protected-data canaries and protocol integration tests. Produce an independent-review packet with exact build/profile scope. Remediate actual findings in tracked child/new work packages and preserve unresolved release gates.
packages.acceptance: No open release-blocking finding or missing required cryptographic production evidence is waived by a green unit test. Independent review is attributed to its actual reviewer, not self-certified. Public-only deployment and protected-production approval remain distinct scopes.
packages.evidence: Security test artifacts, threat-model closure, independent review evidence where required and exact scoped security status.
packages.external_inputs: External expert review is a genuine independent dependency. Continue unrelated work; do not mark the gate complete without its evidence.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Prove durable jobs, backups and disaster recovery
packages.scope: Configure production-capable job execution, lease expiry, retries/dead letters, queue alerts and graceful shutdown. Back up database/content/object manifests and separately authorized recovery material. Rehearse restoring into a clean isolated environment, replaying provider events and rebuilding search/public content. Check actual Neon/Render retention/compute tier before making recovery claims.
packages.acceptance: Process restarts do not lose accepted tasks or double-send effects. A complete restore succeeds with documented key custody and without production PII in CI. Proposed starting objectives are RPO <=24h and RTO <=4h for ordinary operational content; unreconciled accepted financial events must be recoverable from durable/provider records. Objectives require measured proof and budget approval.
packages.evidence: Restore/drill report, outbox/crash tests, backup inventory and documented recovery owners.
packages.external_inputs: Production uptime, backup retention and worker capacity may require a paid plan; no free-tier assumption substitutes for the drill.
packages.implementation_note: Partial foundation implementation; full acceptance and release evidence remain open. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

packages.title: Connect real deployment monitoring and Engine Room freshness
packages.scope: Publish authenticated/internal health summaries for service readiness, deployed SHA, approved content version, queue lag, last successful email/webhook/reconciliation/backup, configured videos, blocked modules and release gates. Connect GitHub events/reconciliation and Render deployment state to Engine Room without sending personal data.
packages.acceptance: Clicking Engine Room refresh retrieves actual available GitHub/deployment state, timestamps success, and retains honest partial-failure/stale indicators. Merged, deployed and live-verified are separate. No private volunteer/donor/report contents appear in status data.
packages.evidence: Observed Engine Room update, refresh/failure tests, deployed-SHA check and data-minimization audit.

packages.title: Run the complete staging acceptance rehearsal
packages.scope: Deploy an isolated production-like staging release and run end-to-end public, volunteer, staff and treasury journeys using synthetic users and processor-approved test mechanisms. Include a new-device recovery exercise, expired activity module, withdrawn document, disabled integration, failed publishing build, provider outage and restored backup.
packages.acceptance: Every launch requirement has demonstrable pass/fail evidence, owner and exact build reference. Test communications cannot reach real supporters. Missing provider credentials or external reviews are visible blockers, not bypassed by a demo flag.
packages.evidence: Acceptance matrix, browser results, content/finance/security signoffs and staging release manifest.

packages.title: Close publication inputs and operational launch gates
packages.scope: Connect and verify the three supplied issue videos, approved bill/downloads and canonical Garden/Cornerstone sites. Confirm current volunteer kits, real contact/privacy channels, media rights, committee/legal wording, current activity modules where activation is intended and all responsible staff. Record any explicitly approved public-preview omissions separately from a full launch.
packages.acceptance: No prototype banner, invented link, missing required media, historic policy mislabeling or fake success remains in the full release. Publication readiness, security readiness and fundraising readiness all have evidence; an inactive optional field program is shown accurately rather than implied active.
packages.evidence: Final content/link/media crawl, launch-gate register and owner/treasurer/security approvals.
packages.external_inputs: Actual policy files, three YouTube links, dedicated-site URLs, sender/domain access, committee setup and required review evidence are unavoidable inputs.

packages.title: Deploy the production release and enable approved functions
packages.scope: Configure verified production domains/TLS, isolated secrets, database/object permissions, sender authentication, backups and monitoring. Apply reversible migrations, publish the immutable content release, deploy portal/API, verify health and enable volunteer/payment/module flags only after their gates pass. Use a rollback checklist and make external provider configuration part of the release.
packages.acceptance: Public pages, real verification mail, authorized materials, protected submissions and permitted donation flow work on the actual production origins. Preview data is absent. Any real-money test is separately authorized and reconciled by the treasurer; no unauthorized card charge is made.
packages.evidence: Production deployment records, domain/TLS checks, smoke results, feature-gate evidence and rollback-ready release record.
packages.external_inputs: DNS/domain control, production credentials and approved recurring operating costs are required before execution.

packages.title: Verify the live site and finish the durable handoff
packages.scope: Rerun critical journeys after production deployment and provider callbacks, verify Engine Room state, inspect errors/deliverability and document observed performance. Deliver operator guides for publishing an issue/video, adding volunteers/staff, activating modules, handling incidents, fundraising reconciliation and restoring service. Update README, AGENTS, changelog, input register and next-maintenance responsibilities.
packages.acceptance: Completion is supported by live evidence, not merely merged PRs. All remaining exceptions are explicit and any additional work is in the denominator. A new agent and a nontechnical campaign operator can continue without this conversation. No unattended ChatGPT scheduler is silently restarted.
packages.evidence: Live acceptance report, final status manifest, operator walkthrough, repository cold-start check and recorded maintenance owners.

packages.title: Individual, revocable private policy-review accounts
packages.scope: Separate website-only Better Auth realm with owner-managed initial passwords, forced replacement, reset, revocation and expiry. No campaign operational grants.
packages.acceptance: Persistent real owner/reviewer journeys, denied privilege/CSRF/financial/portal access, immediate revocation and actual HTTPS checks on the existing authorized preview.
packages.evidence: docs/operations/PRIVATE_REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_20261012.md; docs/operations/PRIVATE_REVIEW_ACCOUNTS.md
packages.external_inputs: Owner claims their own login and supplies reviewer identities privately.
packages.implementation_note: G28-61 scoped acceptance verified on existing HTTPS preview. Original sixty full-launch packages retain their independent acceptance gates.
packages.owner_setup: unclaimed; owner chooses private final credential
